threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think it's acceptable to order a latte at 5 PM. Clue: Not here. It's all about the flat whites or a cheeky pint by then.
Last week on the 3, a guy was juggling oranges in the aisle while rapping about his ex. Only in Brixton, right?

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw a group of kids using an old mattress as a launchpad for their trampoline, I knew I'd found my quirky home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a late-night currywurst joint where the guy behind the counter judges your toppings as seriously as a Michelin chef.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s local when they know to avoid BART on Fridays—forgotten how many of us have had to run for Muni after the Transbay Tube meltdown.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a pigeon hop on the bus today, then walk right off at the next stop. Just another day in the Tenderloin, where even the birds know the route.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all about the plazas and bars, but they miss the small bakeries where locals grab fresh pan con tomate every morning.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell by the way they still check their map app at every corner, as if they might suddenly forget where they are after just one block.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still stand on the wrong side of the escalator at the tube, looking confused when locals rush past. It's like a rite of passage.
Last night on the 196, a bloke serenaded the bus with old jazz tunes, and the driver clapped along. Only in Brixton, eh?

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: Sitting on the terrace, I heard the neighbor's cat and a street musician harmonizing. That's when I realized I belonged here.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You can catch a bus in Friedrichshain, then, just as quickly, find yourself at an underground techno party while it's still daylight. That vibe is a Berlin special.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s local when they instinctively know to avoid BART during rush hour—no amount of overhyped tech can change that chaos.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Just saw a pigeon hop onto the 19 bus and somehow it seemed normal. Only in San Francisco do we have feathered commuters.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is always buzzing, but many afternoons it’s like a ghost town, the locals are inside enjoying their siestas.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell they're the ones still taking a picture of the Casa Ramos sign like it’s a hidden gem, while locals just walk on by.
